options.content:
## Infrastructure
The physical and virtual foundation underneath ClickStack: **Kubernetes node health, host CPU/memory/load, per-volume storage, network, and capacity headroom**. Metrics come from the OpenTelemetry `hostmetrics` and `kubeletstats` receivers and are stored in ClickHouse. **Summary cards are averages or latest values over the selected time range**; charts use automatic Grafana intervals. The **Host** filter narrows host-level (`system.*`) panels, which includes every storage panel; the node status panels (`k8s.node.*`) always show the whole cluster. No data usually means the receiver isn't reporting.

panels.title: Kubernetes nodes Ready %

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 100 * countIf(v = 1) / nullIf(count(), 0) AS value FROM (
  SELECT ResourceAttributes['k8s.node.name'] AS n, argMax(Value, TimeUnix) AS v
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'k8s.node.condition_ready' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix)
  GROUP BY n)

panels.description: Percentage of Kubernetes nodes whose latest Ready condition in the selected range is true. Anything below 100% means at least one node is not accepting workloads.

panels.title: Healthy nodes

targets.rawSql:
SELECT countIf(v = 1) AS value FROM (
  SELECT ResourceAttributes['k8s.node.name'] AS n, argMax(Value, TimeUnix) AS v
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'k8s.node.condition_ready' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix)
  GROUP BY n)

panels.description: Nodes reporting Ready = true on their most recent sample. Compare with the expected cluster size; a drop means capacity was lost.

panels.title: Unhealthy nodes (Not Ready)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT countIf(v != 1) AS value FROM (
  SELECT ResourceAttributes['k8s.node.name'] AS n, argMax(Value, TimeUnix) AS v
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'k8s.node.condition_ready' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix)
  GROUP BY n)

panels.description: Nodes whose latest Ready condition is false or unknown. Any non-zero value is red and should be investigated immediately — pods on that node are not being scheduled.

panels.title: Hosts reporting metrics

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(DISTINCT ResourceAttributes['host.name']) AS value FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge WHERE MetricName = 'system.cpu.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})

panels.description: Distinct selected hosts that reported CPU utilization during the selected time range. Fewer hosts than expected means the host-metrics receiver stopped on one of them.

panels.title: Node status & uptime

targets.rawSql:
SELECT g.node AS "Node",
       if(g.ready = 1, 'Ready', 'Not Ready') AS "Status",
       toUInt64(s.uptime) AS "Uptime"
FROM (
  SELECT ResourceAttributes['k8s.node.name'] AS node,
         argMax(Value, TimeUnix) AS ready
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'k8s.node.condition_ready' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix)
  GROUP BY node) g
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT ResourceAttributes['k8s.node.name'] AS node, argMax(Value, TimeUnix) AS uptime
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'k8s.node.uptime' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix)
  GROUP BY node) s ON g.node = s.node
ORDER BY "Status" DESC, "Uptime" ASC

panels.description: Latest sample per Kubernetes node: Ready status and how long the node has been up. A short uptime after an incident indicates the node rebooted. Per-host CPU and memory are in the Node health section below.

panels.title: Average CPU utilization

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 100 * avg(busy) AS value FROM (
  SELECT ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, Attributes['cpu'] AS cpu, TimeUnix,
         sumIf(Value, Attributes['state'] != 'idle') AS busy
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.cpu.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY host, cpu, TimeUnix)

panels.description: Average non-idle CPU utilization across selected hosts and the full selected time range. Short spikes may be hidden by this average — check the CPU chart below.

panels.title: Average memory utilization

targets.rawSql: SELECT 100 * avgIf(Value, Attributes['state'] = 'used') AS value FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge WHERE MetricName = 'system.memory.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})

panels.description: Average used-memory percentage across selected hosts and the full selected time range. Green below 80%, yellow 80–92%, red 92% or higher.

panels.title: Average 1-minute load

targets.rawSql: SELECT avg(Value) AS value FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge WHERE MetricName = 'system.cpu.load_average.1m' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})

panels.description: Average one-minute system load across selected hosts. Compare each host's load with its CPU-core count; load above the core count means processes are queuing for CPU.

panels.title: Highest inode usage %

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 100 * max(used / nullIf(total, 0)) AS value FROM (
  SELECT host, mountpoint, sumIf(v, st = 'used') AS used, sum(v) AS total FROM (
    SELECT ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, Attributes['mountpoint'] AS mountpoint, Attributes['state'] AS st,
           argMax(Value, TimeUnix) AS v
    FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
    WHERE MetricName = 'system.filesystem.inodes.usage' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
    GROUP BY host, mountpoint, st)
  GROUP BY host, mountpoint)

panels.description: Highest inode consumption of any mounted volume. A filesystem can refuse new files while still reporting free bytes, because it ran out of inodes rather than space — a workload creating very many small files (container layers, ClickHouse parts, log shards) hits this first.

panels.title: CPU utilization by host

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, host, 100 * avg(busy) AS "cpu %" FROM (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, Attributes['cpu'] AS cpu, TimeUnix,
         sumIf(Value, Attributes['state'] != 'idle') AS busy
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.cpu.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY host, cpu, TimeUnix, time)
GROUP BY time, host ORDER BY time

panels.description: Non-idle CPU percentage for each selected host over time. Sustained values above 75% warrant attention; above 90% are critical.

panels.title: Memory utilization by host

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, 100 * avgIf(Value, Attributes['state'] = 'used') AS "mem %"
FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
WHERE MetricName = 'system.memory.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time, host ORDER BY time

panels.description: Used-memory percentage for each selected host over time. Sustained values above 80% warrant attention; above 92% are critical.

panels.title: Load average (1m) by host

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, avg(Value) AS "load 1m"
FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
WHERE MetricName = 'system.cpu.load_average.1m' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time, host ORDER BY time

panels.description: One-minute run-queue length per host. A load consistently above the host CPU-core count means work is waiting for CPU even if utilization looks acceptable.

panels.title: Paging activity by host (per chart interval)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, host, sum(d) AS "page operations" FROM (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host,
         concat(Attributes['direction'], '/', Attributes['type']) AS s,
         max(Value) - min(Value) AS d
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.paging.operations' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY time, host, s)
GROUP BY time, host ORDER BY time

panels.description: Pages moved between memory and disk by each host during each chart interval. This is the memory-pressure signal: a host with ample free memory pages almost never, so a rising line means the working set no longer fits in RAM and the system is trading latency for space. Correlate with the memory chart above.

panels.title: Host averages over selected time range

targets.rawSql:
SELECT c.host AS "Host",
       round(c.cpu, 1) AS "CPU %",
       round(m.mem, 1) AS "Mem %",
       round(m.load, 2) AS "Load 1m",
       round(m.load15, 2) AS "Load 15m"
FROM (
  SELECT host, 100 * avg(busy) AS cpu FROM (
    SELECT ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, Attributes['cpu'] AS cpu, TimeUnix,
         sumIf(Value, Attributes['state'] != 'idle') AS busy
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.cpu.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY host, cpu, TimeUnix)
  GROUP BY host) c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host,
         100 * avgIf(Value, MetricName = 'system.memory.utilization' AND Attributes['state'] = 'used') AS mem,
         avgIf(Value, MetricName = 'system.cpu.load_average.1m') AS load,
         avgIf(Value, MetricName = 'system.cpu.load_average.15m') AS load15
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName IN ('system.memory.utilization', 'system.cpu.load_average.1m', 'system.cpu.load_average.15m') AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY host) m ON c.host = m.host
ORDER BY "CPU %" DESC

panels.description: Per-host averages over the full selected time range, sorted by average CPU utilization. These are not the latest samples.

panels.title: Filesystem used % by volume

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, volume, 100 * (cap - avail) / nullIf(cap, 0) AS "used %" FROM (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, concat(ResourceAttributes['host.name'], ' ', Attributes['mountpoint']) AS volume,
         sumIf(Value, Attributes['state'] = 'free') AS avail, sum(Value) AS cap
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.filesystem.usage' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY time, volume)
WHERE cap > 0 ORDER BY time

panels.description: Percentage of each mounted volume in use, tracked separately per volume rather than rolled up per node — the volume backing container images and the one backing the database fill at completely different rates. Above 80% plan cleanup; above 90% the kubelet starts evicting pods and image pulls fail.

panels.title: Free filesystem capacity by volume

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, concat(ResourceAttributes['host.name'], ' ', Attributes['mountpoint']) AS volume, avgIf(Value, Attributes['state'] = 'free') AS "free"
FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
WHERE MetricName = 'system.filesystem.usage' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
GROUP BY time, volume ORDER BY time

panels.description: Absolute free bytes on each mounted volume. A steadily falling line is the earliest reliable signal that you will run out of disk — extrapolate the slope to estimate when, and act before it reaches zero rather than after.

panels.title: Disk operations by host (per chart interval)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, host, sum(d) AS "operations" FROM (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host,
         concat(Attributes['device'], '/', Attributes['direction']) AS s,
         max(Value) - min(Value) AS d
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.disk.operations' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY time, host, s)
GROUP BY time, host ORDER BY time

panels.description: Read plus write operations completed by each host during each chart interval — the IOPS signal. This is a count per interval, not per second; interval width changes with the time range.

panels.title: Average disk latency by host

targets.rawSql:
SELECT t.time AS time, t.host AS host, 1000 * t.secs / nullIf(o.ops, 0) AS "ms/op"
FROM (
  SELECT time, host, sum(d) AS secs FROM (
    SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host,
           concat(Attributes['device'], '/', Attributes['direction']) AS s,
           max(Value) - min(Value) AS d
    FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
    WHERE MetricName = 'system.disk.operation_time' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
    GROUP BY time, host, s)
  GROUP BY time, host) t
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT time, host, sum(d) AS ops FROM (
    SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host,
           concat(Attributes['device'], '/', Attributes['direction']) AS s,
           max(Value) - min(Value) AS d
    FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
    WHERE MetricName = 'system.disk.operations' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
    GROUP BY time, host, s)
  GROUP BY time, host) o ON t.time = o.time AND t.host = o.host
ORDER BY time

panels.description: Milliseconds of service time per disk operation (operation-time delta divided by operation delta). Unlike the volume charts this value is independent of the chart interval. Single-digit ms is healthy for SSD; a sustained climb means the disk is saturated.

panels.title: Disk I/O volume by host (per chart interval)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, host, sum(d) AS bytes FROM (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host,
         concat(Attributes['device'], '/', Attributes['direction']) AS s,
         max(Value) - min(Value) AS d
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.disk.io' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY time, host, s)
GROUP BY time, host ORDER BY time

panels.description: Combined bytes read and written by each host during each chart interval. This is volume, not bytes per second — a wider time range means wider buckets and larger values.

panels.title: Network I/O volume by host (per chart interval)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, host, sum(d) AS bytes FROM (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host,
         concat(Attributes['device'], '/', Attributes['direction']) AS s,
         max(Value) - min(Value) AS d
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.network.io' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY time, host, s)
GROUP BY time, host ORDER BY time

panels.description: Combined bytes received and transmitted by each host during each chart interval. Use it to spot traffic spikes and to correlate them with latency or error charts.

panels.title: Packets dropped by host (per chart interval)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, host, sum(d) AS "dropped" FROM (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host,
         concat(Attributes['device'], '/', Attributes['direction']) AS s,
         max(Value) - min(Value) AS d
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.network.dropped' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY time, host, s)
GROUP BY time, host ORDER BY time

panels.description: Network packets discarded by each host during each chart interval. Any sustained non-zero value points at buffer exhaustion, NIC saturation, or a misconfigured interface.

panels.title: Network interface errors by host (per chart interval)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, host, sum(d) AS "errors" FROM (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host,
         concat(Attributes['device'], '/', Attributes['direction']) AS s,
         max(Value) - min(Value) AS d
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.network.errors' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY time, host, s)
GROUP BY time, host ORDER BY time

panels.description: Interface-level receive and transmit errors per chart interval. Non-zero values usually indicate a physical problem — cabling, transceiver, or switch port — rather than an application fault.

panels.title: CPU headroom

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 100 - 100 * avg(busy) AS value FROM (
  SELECT ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, Attributes['cpu'] AS cpu, TimeUnix,
         sumIf(Value, Attributes['state'] != 'idle') AS busy
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.cpu.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY host, cpu, TimeUnix)

panels.description: Average unused CPU across selected hosts — how much compute you can still absorb. Below 25% is tight, below 10% means the next workload spike will cause contention.

panels.title: Memory headroom

targets.rawSql: SELECT 100 - 100 * avgIf(Value, Attributes['state'] = 'used') AS value FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge WHERE MetricName = 'system.memory.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})

panels.description: Average unallocated memory across selected hosts. Memory has no equivalent of CPU throttling — running out triggers the OOM killer, so keep this above 20%.

panels.title: Lowest volume free %

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 100 * min(avail / nullIf(cap, 0)) AS value FROM (
  SELECT host, mountpoint, sumIf(v, st = 'free') AS avail, sum(v) AS cap FROM (
    SELECT ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, Attributes['mountpoint'] AS mountpoint, Attributes['state'] AS st,
           argMax(Value, TimeUnix) AS v
    FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
    WHERE MetricName = 'system.filesystem.usage' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
    GROUP BY host, mountpoint, st)
  GROUP BY host, mountpoint)

panels.description: Free-space percentage on the most constrained mounted volume anywhere in the fleet. This is the volume that runs out first, so it governs the whole cluster — and because it is measured per volume rather than per node, a single full data disk cannot be averaged away by healthy volumes on the same node.

panels.title: Total free memory

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum(v) AS value FROM (
  SELECT ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, argMaxIf(Value, TimeUnix, Attributes['state'] = 'free') AS v
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.memory.usage' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY host)

panels.description: Sum of the latest free-memory reading across selected hosts — the memory left for new workloads fleet-wide. Note this is a sum, so a large number can still hide one nearly-full host; check the per-host memory chart before relying on it.

panels.title: CPU & memory headroom over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT c.time AS time, 100 - c.busy AS "CPU headroom %", 100 - m.used AS "Memory headroom %"
FROM (
  SELECT time, 100 * avg(busy) AS busy FROM (
    SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, ResourceAttributes['host.name'] AS host, Attributes['cpu'] AS cpu, TimeUnix,
         sumIf(Value, Attributes['state'] != 'idle') AS busy
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.cpu.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY host, cpu, TimeUnix, time)
  GROUP BY time) c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, 100 * avgIf(Value, Attributes['state'] = 'used') AS used
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_gauge
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.memory.utilization' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY time) m ON c.time = m.time
ORDER BY time

panels.description: Fleet-average spare CPU and spare memory over time. A steady downward slope over days or weeks is the capacity-planning signal — extrapolate it to decide when to add nodes.

panels.title: Free % by volume over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, volume, 100 * avail / nullIf(cap, 0) AS "free %" FROM (
  SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeUnix) AS time, concat(ResourceAttributes['host.name'], ' ', Attributes['mountpoint']) AS volume,
         sumIf(Value, Attributes['state'] = 'free') AS avail, sum(Value) AS cap
  FROM ${database}.otel_metrics_sum
  WHERE MetricName = 'system.filesystem.usage' AND $__timeFilter(TimeUnix) AND ResourceAttributes['host.name'] IN (${host:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY time, volume)
WHERE cap > 0 ORDER BY time

panels.description: Free-space percentage per volume over time. Watch the slope, not the absolute value: a line falling a few percent per day tells you exactly how long you have before cleanup becomes urgent. This is the panel that turns a disk-full outage into a scheduled maintenance task.
